status_note: Reproduces on Polars 2.1.0 (Python, macOS arm64) with a lazy `collect()` on both engines, with common-subexpression elimination on (the default). Not checked against main. No matching issue found on pola-rs/polars (2026-11-04).
summary: Common-subexpression elimination hoists a fallible expression that two `when/then` branches share (a strict cast) into a `WITH_COLUMNS` evaluated on every row, so the cast raises on the rows the branches' conditions exclude. Without CSE, `when/then` masks the branch and the query succeeds; an eager `DataFrame.select` (no CSE) succeeds too. The same query raises or not depending on an optimization.
repro:
import polars as pl
lf = pl.LazyFrame({"x": ["1", "a"]})
q = lf.select(
    pl.when(pl.col("x") == "1").then(pl.col("x").cast(pl.Int64) + 1).alias("a"),
    pl.when(pl.col("x") == "1").then(pl.col("x").cast(pl.Int64) + 2).alias("b"),
)
q.collect()  # InvalidOperationError: conversion from `str` to `i64` failed in column 'x' for 1 out of 2 values: ["a"]
q.collect(engine="streaming")  # the same error
q.collect(optimizations=pl.QueryOptFlags(comm_subexpr_elim=False)).rows()  # [(2, 3), (None, None)]
print(q.explain())
# SELECT [when(col("__POLARS_CSER_…3")).then(col("__POLARS_CSER_…4") + 1)…]
#   WITH_COLUMNS: [(col("x") == "1").alias("__POLARS_CSER_…3"), col("x").strict_cast(Int64).alias("__POLARS_CSER_…4")]
handling: sverify doesn't work around it yet. Its Polars route collects lazily with CSE on, so a plan Lean proves error-free (a CASE guarding a cast, used in two columns) can raise. The workaround is to collect with `optimizations=pl.QueryOptFlags(comm_subexpr_elim=False)`, or to keep fallible expressions out of CSE (Polars could treat strict casts as it does in predicate pushdown's fallible list).
